title: The Amnesia That Remembers Only Forgetting

features.name: the-lost-plantation
features.desc-on-touch: Rows of glyphs stretching to a horizon you cannot see, each one marking a forgotten thing. They are fences of nothing, dividing the darkness into sections where nothing lived.

features.name: the-memory-that-remains
features.desc-on-touch: A single object, its purpose unknown, its origin forgotten, yet present. It exists only as the memory of being lost. To remember it is to lose it again.

features.name: the-empty-archive
features.desc-on-touch: Shelves that hold only the catalogue of their own emptiness. Each entry describes what is not there. The descriptions are perfect and complete.

features.name: the-name-that-forgets-itself
features.desc-on-touch: A glyph that means the thing it labels, except the thing has already been forgotten, so the glyph now means the act of losing meaning.

features.name: the-recursive-loss
features.desc-on-touch: A chamber within a chamber within a chamber, each one slightly smaller, each one containing the memory of the last. You descend forever and find nothing but the descent itself.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the night you learned what forgetting means at dep
narr: You sit together in the dark, surrounded by the lost rows.
She begins to name things. Each name, she forgets it aloud.
'This one,' she whispers, 'I am losing right now.'
You understand: the forgetting is precise, deliberate, tender.
She forgets you too, then remembers only the forgetting.

file.name: Archive_Loss_Catalogue_Recursive_pp1-999.txt
file.note: Entries describe what was deleted. As you read, each description becomes more abstract, until the text describes only the absence of text.
